source.text: Ἀποκάλυψις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἣν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς δεῖξαι τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ, ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει, καὶ ἐσήμανεν ἀποστείλας διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου αὐτοῦ τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ Ἰωάννῃ, ὃς ἐμαρτύρησεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅσα εἶδεν.

records.literal_gloss: Revelation of Jesus Christ, which gave to him the God to show to the slaves of him, what things it is necessary to happen in quickness, and he signified [it] having sent through the angel of him to the slave of him John, \v 2 who testified the word of the God and the testimony of Jesus Christ, as many things as he saw.

en.L: [The] revelation of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, which God gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to show to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves, [the] things that must take place soon; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made [it] known by sending [it] through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave John, \v 2 who bore witness to the word of God and to the testimony of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, all that he saw.
en.B: This is the revelation of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. God gave it to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the things that must happen soon. He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant John and through the angel made these things known. \v 2 John has borne witness to all he saw, to the word of God and the testimony of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: This book is the revelation of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. God gave it to Jesus so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants what is going to happen soon. Jesus sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel to tell it to John, who is also one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants. \v 2 John has told everything he saw. He has passed on the word of God and the testimony that Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} gave.

fr.L: Révélation de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, que Dieu {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a donnée pour montrer à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} esclaves ce qui doit arriver bientôt ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [l’]a fait connaître en [l’]envoyant par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ange à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} esclave Jean, \v 2 qui a rendu témoignage à la parole de Dieu et au témoignage de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, tout ce qu’il a vu.
fr.B: Voici la révélation de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Dieu la {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a donnée pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} montre à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs ce qui doit arriver bientôt. Il a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ange à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur Jean et, par cet ange, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui a fait connaître ces choses. \v 2 Jean a rendu témoignage à tout ce qu’il a vu, à la parole de Dieu et au témoignage de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Ce livre est la révélation de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Dieu l’a donnée à Jésus pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} montre à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs ce qui va bientôt arriver. Jésus a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ange pour l’annoncer à Jean, qui est lui aussi l’un de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs. \v 2 Jean a raconté tout ce qu’il a vu. Il a transmis la parole de Dieu et le témoignage que Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} a donné.

es.L: [La] revelación de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, que Dios {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dio para mostrar a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} esclavos las cosas que deben suceder pronto; y [la] dio a conocer enviándo[la] por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ángel a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} esclavo Juan, \v 2 el cual dio testimonio de la palabra de Dios y del testimonio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, de todo lo que vio.
es.B: Esta es la revelación de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Dios {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} la dio para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mostrara a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} siervos lo que tiene que suceder pronto. Envió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ángel a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} siervo Juan y por medio del ángel dio a conocer estas cosas. \v 2 Juan ha dado testimonio de todo lo que vio: de la palabra de Dios y del testimonio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Este libro es la revelación de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Dios dio este mensaje a Jesús para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pudiera mostrar a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} siervos lo que va a suceder pronto. Jesús envió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ángel para contárselo a Juan, que también es uno de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} siervos. \v 2 Juan ha contado todo lo que vio. Ha transmitido la palabra de Dios y el testimonio que dio {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Ufunuo wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ambao Mungu alimpa ili awaonyeshe watumwa {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mambo ambayo lazima yatukie upesi; {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} aliyajulisha kwa kumtuma malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Yohana, \v 2 ambaye alilishuhudia neno la Mungu na ushuhuda wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, yote aliyoyaona.
sw.B: Huu ni ufunuo wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Mungu alimpa ufunuo huu ili awaonyeshe watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mambo ambayo lazima yatokee hivi karibuni. Alimtuma malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Yohana, na kupitia malaika huyo akayajulisha mambo hayo. \v 2 Yohana ameshuhudia yote aliyoyaona, yaani neno la Mungu na ushuhuda wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Kitabu hiki ni ufunuo wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Mungu alimpa Yesu ufunuo huu ili awaonyeshe watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mambo yatakayotokea hivi karibuni. Yesu alimtuma malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} amweleze Yohana, ambaye pia ni mmoja wa watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. \v 2 Yohana amewaambia watu yote aliyoyaona. Amelieleza neno la Mungu na ushuhuda ambao Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} aliutoa.

decisions.choice: the revelation that comes from Jesus Christ: he is the one who makes it known
alternatives: the revelation about Jesus Christ: he is its subject
decisions.reason: The genitive can mean either. The rest of the sentence says how the revelation came: God gave it to Jesus, and Jesus made it known through his angel to John. So Jesus is first of all the one who reveals. He is also at the center of what is revealed (1:12-18), and the phrase may hold both. The word Ἀποκάλυψις means an uncovering of what was hidden, and from it the book takes its name, "Revelation" or "Apocalypse".

decisions.choice: an echo of Daniel 2:28-29: what must happen
decisions.reason: δεῖ γενέσθαι, "must happen", recalls Daniel 2:28-29, where Daniel tells the king that God has made known what will happen in the last days. In Daniel the events lie in the distant future; here they are coming ἐν τάχει. "Must" speaks of what God has determined, not of mere likelihood.

decisions.choice: soon: the events are about to begin
alternatives: quickly or suddenly: when they come, they will come fast
decisions.reason: ἐν τάχει can mean "in a short time" or "with speed". Verse 3 says "the time is near", and the book closes with "I am coming soon" (22:7, 12, 20), which points to nearness in time. The phrase does not say how long the whole series of events will last.

decisions.choice: slaves: people who belong wholly to their master
decisions.reason: δούλοις and δούλῳ are the ordinary words for slaves, people owned by a master and bound to do his will. Applied to believers and to John, they mean that they belong to God and to Christ, not to themselves. The prophets of Israel were called God's slaves in the same way (Amos 3:7; Revelation 10:7).

decisions.choice: made known through signs: the message is given in pictures and symbols
alternatives: simply "made known", with no thought of signs
decisions.reason: ἐσήμανεν is related to the word for a sign, and it often means to make something known by a sign or a picture. The book that follows shows its message mostly through visions and symbols, so the word fits it well. But it is also used for making known in general, so the point should not be pressed.

decisions.choice: the testimony of Jesus: the testimony that Jesus himself gave
alternatives: the testimony about Jesus, given by believers
decisions.reason: "Of Jesus Christ" can name the one who gives the testimony or the one it is about. Verse 5 calls Jesus "the faithful witness", which favors the testimony he gave, and that is the reading taken here. The two are close, since what Jesus testified is what John testifies to. The phrase recurs in 1:9; 12:17; 19:10; 20:4.

decisions.choice: servants, servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m4) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable name the angel and John as separate steps
decisions.reason: The Greek packs the sending and the making known into one clause. Balanced and Readable split it into two clauses so that the line from God to Jesus to the angel to John is easy to follow.

decisions.choice: "Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" (L), "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in the letters: the title is under the christos setting wherever the English has it. French writes "Jésus Christ" without the usual hyphen so that "Jésus le Messie" reads naturally as the alternative; Literal keeps the bare title, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: esclaves, esclave (L); serviteurs, serviteur (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the English and the style guide: Literal keeps "esclave" for a person wholly owned by a master (m4); Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", which in French does not carry modern ideas of the slave trade, while the meaning decision keeps the sense of belonging.

decisions.choice: subject pronouns for God and Christ left unexpressed; object and possessive pronouns carry the span (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: Spanish shows the subject in the verb ending and normally leaves out "él". Where the English has a deity_pronoun span on "he" as subject, Spanish usually has no pronoun and so no span; one is written, with the span, only where Spanish needs it for clarity ("para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mostrara"). Object, possessive and prepositional pronouns ("le", "se", "lo", "su", "me", "mi", "a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}", "te", "tu") always carry the span, at every level; Jesus's own "yo" and the joined forms "conmigo", "contigo" have none.

decisions.choice: revelación
decisions.reason: Spanish readers know the book as "Apocalipsis", but in everyday Spanish "apocalipsis" has come to mean a catastrophe. The word here names the act of uncovering what was hidden, which "revelación" says plainly at every level.

decisions.choice: ufunuo
decisions.reason: "Ufunuo" (an uncovering, a making known) is the noun for what is revealed, and it names the book. "Maono" (visions) would describe only the way the message came, not that it is a disclosure from Jesus (m1).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} and other free pronouns and possessives only
alternatives: a span on every pronoun, as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God and Christ inside the verb ("alimpa", "awaonyeshe"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns, the joined forms (naye, kwake) and the possessives, as in the rest of the Swahili New Testament. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English in Revelation.

source.text: μακάριος ὁ ἀναγινώσκων καὶ οἱ ἀκούοντες τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας καὶ τηροῦντες τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ γεγραμμένα, ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς ἐγγύς.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the [one] reading and those hearing the words of the prophecy and keeping the things in it having been written, for the time [is] near.

en.L: Blessed [is] the one who reads and those who hear the words of the prophecy and keep the things written in it, for the time [is] near.
en.B: How blessed is the one who reads the words of this prophecy aloud, and those who hear them and keep what is written here! The time is near.
en.R: God blesses the person who reads this prophecy aloud to the church. He blesses those who listen to it and do what it says. The time when these things will happen is near.

fr.L: Heureux celui qui lit et ceux qui entendent les paroles de la prophétie et gardent ce qui y est écrit, car le temps [est] proche.
fr.B: Heureux celui qui lit à haute voix les paroles de cette prophétie, et heureux ceux qui les entendent et gardent ce qui y est écrit ! Car le temps est proche.
fr.R: Dieu bénit celui qui lit cette prophétie à haute voix devant l’église. Il bénit ceux qui l’écoutent et qui font ce qu’elle dit. Le moment où tout cela va arriver est proche.

es.L: Dichoso el que lee y los que oyen las palabras de la profecía y guardan las cosas escritas en ella, porque el tiempo [está] cerca.
es.B: ¡Qué dichoso es el que lee en voz alta las palabras de esta profecía, y dichosos los que las oyen y guardan lo que aquí está escrito! El tiempo está cerca.
es.R: Dios bendice a la persona que lee esta profecía en voz alta a la iglesia. Bendice a los que la escuchan y hacen lo que dice. Ya está cerca el tiempo en que todo esto va a suceder.

sw.L: Heri yeye anayesoma na wale wanaosikia maneno ya unabii huu na kuyashika yaliyoandikwa ndani yake, kwa maana wakati [uko] karibu.
sw.B: Heri mtu anayesoma kwa sauti maneno ya unabii huu, na heri wale wanaoyasikia na kuyashika yaliyoandikwa humu! Wakati umekaribia.
sw.R: Mungu humbariki mtu anayelisomea kanisa unabii huu kwa sauti. Huwabariki pia wale wanaousikiliza na kufanya yale unayosema. Wakati ambapo mambo haya yatatokea umekaribia.

decisions.choice: one person reads the book aloud to a gathered church, and the rest listen
decisions.reason: The reader is singular and the hearers are plural. Books were read aloud in the meeting of the church (Colossians 4:16; 1 Thessalonians 5:27), and most believers heard Scripture rather than read it for themselves.

decisions.choice: the first of seven blessings in the book
decisions.reason: μακάριος opens a pronouncement of blessing, as in Psalm 1:1 and Matthew 5:3-11. Revelation has seven of them (1:3; 14:13; 16:15; 19:9; 20:6; 22:7, 14). Each says who is in a happy state before God, not merely who feels happy.

decisions.choice: keep: hold fast to what the book says and live by it
decisions.reason: τηροῦντες means to keep or observe. With words as its object it means to heed and obey them, as in 22:7 and John 14:23. The book warns elsewhere against changing its words (22:18-19), but that is not the point here.

decisions.choice: the time: the appointed time when these things happen
decisions.reason: καιρὸς is time seen as a season or a set moment, not as a length of time. It refers to the time God has set for the events the book reveals (compare 22:10).

decisions.choice: aloud (B, R)
decisions.reason: In English "the one who reads" sounds like private reading. Balanced and Readable add "aloud" because the reader here reads to others (see the culture decision). Readable also adds "to the church".

decisions.choice: God blesses (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who gives the blessing, which the passive form "blessed" implies, so that a young reader does not take "blessed" as a feeling.

decisions.choice: "Heureux" (L, B); "Dieu bénit" (R) (for the seven blessings of the book)
decisions.reason: The word declares someone fortunate in God's sight. "Heureux" is the established French word for such sayings; "béni" would rather answer a different Greek word ("blessed" as praised), and "bienheureux" now sounds churchly. Readable names God as the one who blesses, as the English Readable does, so that "heureux" is not read as a passing feeling.

decisions.choice: dichoso
decisions.reason: "Bienaventurado" is the older church word and sounds dated to many readers; "bendito" is the word for blessing spoken by God or to God. "Dichoso" is the settled Spanish word for this kind of blessing in the Gospels and keeps the sense of a happy, favored state. Readable says who gives the blessing, as the English does.

decisions.choice: heri
decisions.reason: "Heri" is the Swahili word for the pronouncement "blessed is ...", as in the Gospels; it is the first of the book's seven blessings (m2). Readable says plainly that God blesses, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Ἰωάννης ταῖς ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαις ταῖς ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἑπτὰ πνευμάτων ἃ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀπὸ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ μάρτυς ὁ πιστός, ὁ πρωτότοκος τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ ὁ ἄρχων τῶν βασιλέων τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: John to the seven churches the in the Asia: grace to you and peace from the [one] being and the [one who] was and the [one] coming, and from the seven spirits which [are] before the throne of him, \v 5 and from Jesus Christ, the witness the faithful, the firstborn of the dead and the ruler of the kings of the earth.

en.L: John, to the seven churches that [are] in Asia: grace to you and peace from the one who is and who was and who is coming, and from the seven spirits that [are] before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne, \v 5 and from Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead and the ruler of the kings of the earth.
en.B: From John, to the seven churches in the province of Asia. Grace to you and peace from the one who is, who was, and who is coming; from the seven spirits that are before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne; \v 5 and from Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the witness who is faithful, the firstborn from among the dead, and the ruler over the kings of the earth.
en.R: From John, to the seven churches in the province of Asia. May grace and peace come to you from God, the one who is, who always was, and who is coming. May they come from the seven spirits in front of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne, \v 5 and from Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Jesus is the witness who can be trusted. He was the first to be raised from the dead to new life, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules over the kings of the earth.

fr.L: Jean, aux sept églises qui [sont] en Asie : grâce à vous et paix de la part de celui qui est et qui était et qui vient, et de la part des sept esprits qui [sont] devant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trône, \v 5 et de la part de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le témoin fidèle, le premier-né des morts et le chef des rois de la terre.
fr.B: De la part de Jean, aux sept églises de la province d’Asie. Grâce et paix à vous de la part de celui qui est, qui était et qui vient, de la part des sept esprits qui sont devant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trône, \v 5 et de la part de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, le témoin fidèle, le premier-né d’entre les morts et le souverain des rois de la terre.
fr.R: De la part de Jean, aux sept églises de la province d’Asie. Que la grâce et la paix vous soient données par Dieu, celui qui est, qui a toujours été et qui vient. Qu’elles vous soient données aussi par les sept esprits qui se tiennent devant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trône, \v 5 et par Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Jésus est le témoin digne de confiance. Il a été le premier à être relevé d’entre les morts pour une vie nouvelle, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} règne sur les rois de la terre.

es.L: Juan, a las siete iglesias que [están] en Asia: gracia a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y paz de parte del que es y del que era y del que viene, y de parte de los siete espíritus que [están] delante de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} trono, \v 5 y de parte de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, el testigo fiel, el primogénito de los muertos y el soberano de los reyes de la tierra.
es.B: De Juan, a las siete iglesias de la provincia de Asia. Gracia y paz a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} de parte del que es, del que era y del que viene; de parte de los siete espíritus que están delante de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} trono, \v 5 y de parte de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, el testigo que es fiel, el primogénito de entre los muertos y el soberano de los reyes de la tierra.
es.R: De Juan, a las siete iglesias de la provincia de Asia. Que la gracia y la paz vengan sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} de parte de Dios, el que es, el que siempre ha sido y el que viene. Que vengan de los siete espíritus que están delante de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} trono, \v 5 y de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Jesús es el testigo en quien se puede confiar. Fue el primero en resucitar de entre los muertos a una vida nueva, y gobierna sobre los reyes de la tierra.

sw.L: Yohana, kwa makanisa saba yaliyo katika Asia: neema kwenu na amani kutoka kwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyepo na aliyekuwepo na anayekuja, na kutoka kwa roho saba zilizo mbele ya kiti {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} cha enzi, \v 5 na kutoka kwa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, shahidi mwaminifu, mzaliwa wa kwanza wa wafu, na mtawala wa wafalme wa dunia.
sw.B: Kutoka kwa Yohana, kwa makanisa saba yaliyo katika jimbo la Asia. Neema na amani ziwe kwenu kutoka kwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyepo, aliyekuwepo, na anayekuja; kutoka kwa roho saba zilizo mbele ya kiti {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} cha enzi; \v 5 na kutoka kwa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, shahidi aliye mwaminifu, mzaliwa wa kwanza kutoka kwa wafu, na mtawala juu ya wafalme wa dunia.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa Yohana, kwa makanisa saba yaliyo katika jimbo la Asia. Neema na amani ziwe kwenu kutoka kwa Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyepo, aliyekuwepo tangu zamani zote, na anayekuja. Ziwe kwenu pia kutoka kwa roho saba zilizo mbele ya kiti {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} cha enzi, \v 5 na kutoka kwa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Yesu ni shahidi anayeaminika. Yeye ndiye wa kwanza kufufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu kwa uzima mpya, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anawatawala wafalme wa dunia.

decisions.choice: Asia: the Roman province in the west of what is now Turkey
decisions.reason: Ἀσίᾳ was the name of a Roman province on the Aegean coast, with Ephesus as its leading city. The seven churches named in 1:11 are all in it.

decisions.choice: the title of God is kept whole, as a name that does not change
decisions.reason: After ἀπὸ, "from", Greek grammar expects the words that follow to change their form, but John keeps them in the form of a subject: "from the one who is". He treats the whole phrase as a fixed name of God, one that no grammar may alter. This is deliberate; John writes the regular form elsewhere.

decisions.choice: an echo of God's name in Exodus 3:14, and a God who is coming
decisions.reason: "The one who is" recalls God's words to Moses in Exodus 3:14, "I am who I am", which the Greek translation of the Old Testament renders "I am the one who is". The third part is not "who will be" but ὁ ἐρχόμενος, "who is coming": God's future is his coming to the world (1:7-8). The same title recurs in 1:8 and 4:8.

decisions.choice: the seven spirits: the Spirit of God in his fullness
alternatives: seven angels or spirits who stand before God's throne
decisions.reason: Grace and peace come from God, from the seven spirits, and from Jesus Christ, which suggests that the seven spirits stand for the Spirit of God. Seven is the number of completeness in the book, and Zechariah 4:2, 10 speaks of seven lamps that are the eyes of the Lord; Isaiah 11:2 names the Spirit's gifts. Elsewhere Revelation speaks of the seven spirits before the throne (3:1; 4:5; 5:6). Some take them to be seven angels, since angels stand before God (8:2). The text does not decide it.

decisions.choice: firstborn of the dead: the first to rise from death to the life that does not end
decisions.reason: πρωτότοκος can mean first in time and first in rank. Jesus is the first to be raised from the dead and never die again, and his rising gives him the place of honor (compare Colossians 1:18 and Psalm 89:28, where the king is God's firstborn, "highest of the kings of the earth").

decisions.choice: an echo of Psalm 89
decisions.reason: The three titles recall Psalm 89, where God promises David's line a "firstborn", "highest of the kings of the earth" (89:27), and a throne as lasting as "the faithful witness in the sky" (89:37). John applies these promises to Jesus.

decisions.choice: the province of Asia (B, R)
decisions.reason: To an English reader "Asia" means the continent. Balanced and Readable add "the province of" to show that a Roman province is meant (see m1).

decisions.choice: May grace and peace come ... from God (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek greeting has no verb. Readable makes it a wish, as such greetings were, and names God, since the title that follows is his (m3).

decisions.choice: seven spirits, lowercase (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: A capital would decide the question that m4 leaves open, so every level writes "seven spirits" in lowercase.

decisions.choice: "les sept églises", lowercase (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide has it, "l'Église" with a capital is the whole body of believers, and "l'église" one congregation. Each of the seven churches is a congregation in a city, so the word is lowercase throughout Revelation.

decisions.choice: gracia a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: The greeting is to the seven churches together, so "you" is plural and takes the plural_you span, Latin American "ustedes" by default and "vosotros" as the alternative. The same holds wherever the book speaks to more than one person.

decisions.choice: el soberano de los reyes
decisions.reason: "Príncipe" now suggests a king's son rather than a ruler. "Soberano" names the one who rules over the kings themselves; Readable says it with a verb, "gobierna sobre".

decisions.choice: aliyepo, aliyekuwepo, na anayekuja
decisions.reason: Three relative verbs keep God's title whole as a fixed name (m2). "Anayekuja" keeps the Greek present, a God who is already on his way (m3), where a future "atakayekuja" would put his coming only later.

source.text: Τῷ ἀγαπῶντι ἡμᾶς καὶ λύσαντι ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ αἵματι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐποίησεν ἡμᾶς βασιλείαν, ἱερεῖς τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.

records.literal_gloss: To the [one] loving us and having freed us from the sins of us in the blood of him \v 6 and he made us a kingdom, priests to the God and Father of him, to him the glory and the might into the ages of the ages; amen.

en.L: To the one who loves us and freed us from our sins by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood \v 6 —and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made us a kingdom, priests to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} God and Father—to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [be] the glory and the might for the ages of the ages. Amen.
en.B: To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who loves us and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood released us from our sins, \v 6 and who made us a kingdom, priests in the service of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} God and Father—to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be glory and power forever and ever. Amen.
en.R: Jesus loves us, and by shedding {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has set us free from our sins. \v 6 He has made us into a kingdom. We are priests who serve {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} God and Father. May glory and power be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} forever and ever! Amen.

fr.L: À celui qui nous aime et qui nous a délivrés de nos péchés par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang \v 6 — et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait de nous un royaume, des prêtres pour {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Dieu et Père — à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} la gloire et la puissance pour les siècles des siècles. Amen.
fr.B: À celui qui nous aime, qui nous a délivrés de nos péchés par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang \v 6 et qui a fait de nous un royaume, des prêtres au service de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Dieu et Père, à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} soient la gloire et la puissance pour toujours et à jamais ! Amen.
fr.R: Jésus nous aime, et en versant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a libérés de nos péchés. \v 6 Il a fait de nous un royaume. Nous sommes des prêtres qui servent {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Dieu et Père. À {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} la gloire et la puissance, pour toujours et à jamais ! Amen.

es.L: Al que nos ama y nos libró de nuestros pecados con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sangre \v 6 —y nos hizo un reino, sacerdotes para {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Dios y Padre—, a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [sea] la gloria y el dominio por los siglos de los siglos. Amén.
es.B: Al que nos ama y con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sangre nos liberó de nuestros pecados, \v 6 y que nos hizo un reino, sacerdotes al servicio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Dios y Padre, ¡a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sea la gloria y el poder por los siglos de los siglos! Amén.
es.R: Jesús nos ama, y derramando {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sangre nos ha liberado de nuestros pecados. \v 6 Ha hecho de nosotros un reino. Somos sacerdotes que sirven a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Dios y Padre. ¡Que la gloria y el poder sean {{deity_pronoun:suyos|Suyos}} para siempre! Amén.

sw.L: Kwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayetupenda na aliyetufungua kutoka katika dhambi zetu kwa damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} \v 6 —{{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} alitufanya kuwa ufalme, makuhani kwa Mungu na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}—kwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [uwe] utukufu na uweza hata zama za zama. Amina.
sw.B: Kwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayetupenda, na aliyetuweka huru mbali na dhambi zetu kwa damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \v 6 na aliyetufanya kuwa ufalme, makuhani wanaomtumikia Mungu na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: utukufu na uweza viwe {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} milele na milele. Amina.
sw.R: Yesu anatupenda, na kwa kumwaga damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ametuweka huru mbali na dhambi zetu. \v 6 Ametufanya kuwa ufalme. Sisi ni makuhani tunaomtumikia Mungu na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Utukufu na uweza viwe {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}} milele na milele! Amina.

decisions.choice: freed us from our sins
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads λύσαντι, "freed". Many later manuscripts have a word that differs by one letter and means "washed" (compare 7:14, "washed their robes"). The older manuscripts support "freed", and the translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a present love and a finished deliverance
decisions.reason: ἀγαπῶντι, "loves", is present: his love goes on. λύσαντι, "freed", is past: the deliverance was done once, by his death. John then breaks off the pattern of the sentence and goes on with a plain past verb, ἐποίησεν, "and he made us".

decisions.choice: by his blood: the price or the means of the release
alternatives: in his blood, as the place where it happens
decisions.reason: ἐν with "blood" here gives the means, as in 5:9, where the Lamb bought people for God "by your blood". His blood stands for his death.

decisions.choice: an echo of Exodus 19:6: a kingdom of priests
decisions.reason: At Sinai God called Israel "a kingdom of priests and a holy nation" (Exodus 19:6). Revelation gives the same calling to all whom Christ has freed, from every people (5:9-10; 20:6; compare 1 Peter 2:9). As priests they have access to God and serve him.

decisions.choice: a doxology: a wish or a statement that glory belongs to him
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb. Such sentences may be read "be his" or "is his"; the difference is small, since praise wishes what is already true. "For the ages of the ages" is the Greek way of saying forever. ἀμήν, "amen", is a Hebrew word meaning "it is true, so let it be", said to agree with what has just been said.

decisions.choice: Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks of "the one who loves us", and the last person named was Jesus Christ (1:5). Readable names him and turns the long doxology into short sentences.

decisions.choice: dashes around "and he made us ..." (L)
decisions.reason: Literal marks the break in the sentence (m2) with dashes; Balanced and Readable smooth it into the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" included (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in the letters: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for God or Christ carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and so do "le", "lui", "l'", "son", "sa", "ses", and the "moi", "me", "ma", "mon" with which Jesus speaks of himself. A possessive agrees with the thing possessed ("{{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang", "{{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main"). A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: por los siglos de los siglos (L, B); para siempre (R)
alternatives: por las edades de las edades
decisions.reason: "Por los siglos de los siglos" is the Spanish doxology formula already used in Galatians, Philippians and 1 Peter, and it keeps the doubled "ages" at Literal and Balanced. Readable says plainly "para siempre", as the English Readable says "forever and ever".

decisions.choice: hata zama za zama (L); milele na milele (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of ages upon ages with "zama", the word used for "age" in the Swahili New Testament; Balanced and Readable use the everyday "milele na milele" (forever and ever).

source.text: Ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται μετὰ τῶν νεφελῶν, καὶ ὄψεται αὐτὸν πᾶς ὀφθαλμὸς καὶ οἵτινες αὐτὸν ἐξεκέντησαν, καὶ κόψονται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Behold he comes with the clouds, and will see him every eye and [those] who him pierced, and will mourn over him all the tribes of the earth.

en.L: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and those who pierced {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Look! He is coming with the clouds. Every eye will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, those who pierced {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among them, and all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts in grief over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Look! Jesus is coming with the clouds. Everyone will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, including the people who pierced {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. All the peoples of the earth will cry out in grief over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Voici, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vient avec les nuées, et tout œil {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verra, et ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont transpercé, et toutes les tribus de la terre se lamenteront sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Voici qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vient avec les nuées ! Tous les yeux {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verront, même ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont transpercé, et toutes les tribus de la terre se frapperont la poitrine de douleur à cause de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Regardez ! Jésus vient avec les nuages. Tout le monde {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verra, même ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont transpercé. Tous les peuples de la terre pleureront de douleur à cause de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, viene con las nubes, y todo ojo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} verá, y los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} traspasaron, y todas las tribus de la tierra harán lamento por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! Viene con las nubes. Todo ojo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} verá, también los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} traspasaron, y todas las tribus de la tierra se golpearán el pecho de dolor por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! Jesús viene con las nubes. Todos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} verán, también los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} traspasaron. Todos los pueblos de la tierra llorarán con gran dolor por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Tazama, anakuja pamoja na mawingu, na kila jicho litamwona, na wale waliomchoma, na makabila yote ya dunia yataomboleza kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Tazama! Anakuja pamoja na mawingu. Kila jicho litamwona, hata wale waliomchoma, na makabila yote ya dunia yatajipiga vifua kwa huzuni kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Tazama! Yesu anakuja pamoja na mawingu. Kila mtu atamwona, hata watu wale waliomchoma. Watu wote wa dunia watalia kwa huzuni kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: an echo of Daniel 7:13: one who comes with the clouds
decisions.reason: In Daniel 7:13 one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of Days and receives an everlasting kingdom. Jesus used the same words of himself (Matthew 24:30; 26:64). Here they describe Jesus's coming; verse 13 takes up Daniel's "one like a son of man".

decisions.choice: an echo of Zechariah 12:10-14: the one they pierced, and mourning by tribes
decisions.reason: Zechariah 12:10-14 says the people will look on the one they have pierced and mourn for him, family by family, every tribe of the land. John 19:37 quotes the same verse of Jesus's death. Revelation widens it from the tribes of the land to all the tribes of the earth.

decisions.choice: the tribes of the earth: all the peoples of the world
alternatives: the tribes of the land of Israel, as in Zechariah
decisions.reason: γῆς can mean the whole earth or a land. Zechariah meant the land of Israel, but "every eye" in the same sentence points to the whole world, and Revelation uses the phrase for all the earth's peoples (5:9; 7:9; 14:6).

decisions.choice: mourn over him: grief at his coming, whether it leads to repentance or to dismay
alternatives: mourning that is terror at judgment
decisions.reason: κόψονται means to beat the breast in mourning. In Zechariah the mourning goes with repentance, and Revelation hopes for the nations to turn (11:13; 14:6-7; 15:4). But elsewhere in the book the earth's peoples mourn as judgment comes (18:9). This sentence does not say which mourning is meant.

decisions.choice: Look
decisions.reason: The style guide does not use "behold". "Look" keeps the call to attention.

decisions.choice: Jesus; Everyone (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, which the context makes plain (1:5), and turns "every eye" into "everyone", which is what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: "Voici" (L, B); "Regardez !" (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: Unlike the English "behold", "voici" is current French and keeps the call to attention, so Literal and Balanced use it. Readable uses the plain imperative, as the English Readable says "Look!".

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}
decisions.reason: The call to look is spoken to the readers of the churches, so Spanish uses the plural imperative with the plural_you span. "He aquí" belongs to narrative at Literal; here John speaks directly to his hearers.

decisions.choice: a double yes, in Greek and in Hebrew
decisions.reason: ναί is the Greek for "yes" and ἀμήν the Hebrew word that means the same. Together they make a strong agreement: this will surely happen. The same pairing comes in 22:20.

decisions.choice: this will happen (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the "yes" agrees to.

source.text: Ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ, λέγει κύριος, ὁ θεός, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, ὁ παντοκράτωρ.

records.literal_gloss: I am the Alpha and the O, says [the] Lord the God, the [one] being and the [one who] was and the [one] coming, the Almighty.

en.L: "I am the Alpha and the Omega," says [the] Lord God, the one who is and who was and who is coming, the Almighty.
en.B: "I am the Alpha and the Omega," says the Lord God—the one who is, who was, and who is coming, the Almighty.
en.R: "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end of all things," says the Lord God. He is the one who is, who always was, and who is coming. He is the Almighty.

fr.L: « Je suis l’Alpha et l’Oméga », dit le Seigneur Dieu, celui qui est et qui était et qui vient, le Tout-Puissant.
fr.B: « Je suis l’Alpha et l’Oméga », dit le Seigneur Dieu, celui qui est, qui était et qui vient, le Tout-Puissant.
fr.R: « Je suis l’Alpha et l’Oméga, le commencement et la fin de toutes choses », dit le Seigneur Dieu. Il est celui qui est, qui a toujours été et qui vient. Il est le Tout-Puissant.

es.L: «Yo soy el Alfa y la Omega», dice [el] Señor Dios, el que es y el que era y el que viene, el Todopoderoso.
es.B: «Yo soy el Alfa y la Omega», dice el Señor Dios, el que es, el que era y el que viene, el Todopoderoso.
es.R: «Yo soy el Alfa y la Omega, el principio y el fin de todas las cosas», dice el Señor Dios. Él es el que es, el que siempre ha sido y el que viene. Él es el Todopoderoso.

sw.L: "Mimi ni Alfa na Omega," anasema Bwana Mungu, aliyepo na aliyekuwepo na anayekuja, Mwenyezi.
sw.B: "Mimi ni Alfa na Omega," anasema Bwana Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyepo, aliyekuwepo, na anayekuja, Mwenyezi.
sw.R: "Mimi ni Alfa na Omega, mwanzo na mwisho wa vitu vyote," anasema Bwana Mungu. Yeye ndiye aliyepo, aliyekuwepo tangu zamani zote, na anayekuja. Yeye ndiye Mwenyezi.

decisions.choice: the Alpha and the Omega: the first and the last of all things
decisions.reason: Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet. God is the source of all things and their goal, before everything and after it. Revelation explains the phrase itself: "the beginning and the end" (21:6), "the first and the last" (22:13). In 22:13 Jesus says the same of himself.

decisions.choice: the Almighty: the one who rules over all
decisions.reason: παντοκράτωρ means the ruler of all. In the Greek Old Testament it renders the Hebrew titles "LORD of hosts" and "Shaddai". With "Lord God" it echoes the prophets' "the LORD God of hosts" (for example Amos 4:13). It recurs nine times in Revelation and once elsewhere in the New Testament (2 Corinthians 6:18).

decisions.choice: God speaks: the speaker is the Lord God
decisions.reason: λέγει names the speaker as the Lord God, and the title that follows is the one used of God in 1:4. In 22:13 Jesus takes the title "the Alpha and the Omega" for himself, so the book counts him with God, but here the words are given as God's.

decisions.choice: the beginning and the end of all things (R)
decisions.reason: A reader who does not know Greek will not know what the letter names mean. Readable adds their meaning, using the explanation Revelation itself gives in 21:6 and 22:13.

decisions.choice: el Todopoderoso
decisions.reason: "Todopoderoso" is the plain Spanish title for God as the one who holds power over all, and it is the word the Spanish Gospels already use. "Omnipotente" is a learned word that new readers may not know.

decisions.choice: Mwenyezi
decisions.reason: "Mwenyezi" is the established Swahili title for God as the one who holds all power and rules over all (m2), understood by every reader; it is used for the same title through the book.

source.text: Ἐγὼ Ἰωάννης, ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὑμῶν καὶ συγκοινωνὸς ἐν τῇ θλίψει καὶ βασιλείᾳ καὶ ὑπομονῇ ἐν Ἰησοῦ, ἐγενόμην ἐν τῇ νήσῳ τῇ καλουμένῃ Πάτμῳ διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: I John, the brother of you and fellow-sharer in the affliction and kingdom and endurance in Jesus, came to be in the island the [one] being called Patmos because of the word of the God and the testimony of Jesus.

en.L: I, John, your brother and fellow sharer in the affliction and kingdom and endurance in Jesus, came to be on the island called Patmos because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.
en.B: I, John, am your brother, and in Jesus I share with you the affliction, the kingdom, and the endurance. It was because of God's word and the testimony of Jesus that I came to be on the island called Patmos.
en.R: I am John, your brother. Because we belong to Jesus, we share the same troubles. We share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom, and we share the strength to keep going. I was on the island of Patmos because I had spoken God's word and the testimony of Jesus.

fr.L: Moi, Jean, votre frère et compagnon dans la détresse, le royaume et la persévérance en Jésus, je me trouvai dans l’île appelée Patmos à cause de la parole de Dieu et du témoignage de Jésus.
fr.B: Moi, Jean, je suis votre frère, et en Jésus je partage avec vous la détresse, le royaume et la persévérance. C’est à cause de la parole de Dieu et du témoignage de Jésus que je me trouvai dans l’île qu’on appelle Patmos.
fr.R: Je suis Jean, votre frère. Parce que nous appartenons à Jésus, nous connaissons les mêmes souffrances. Nous avons part à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume, et nous recevons la même force pour tenir bon. J’étais dans l’île de Patmos parce que j’avais annoncé la parole de Dieu et le témoignage de Jésus.

es.L: Yo, Juan, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} hermano y compañero en la aflicción y [en el] reino y [en la] perseverancia en Jesús, llegué a estar en la isla llamada Patmos a causa de la palabra de Dios y del testimonio de Jesús.
es.B: Yo, Juan, soy {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} hermano, y en Jesús comparto con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la aflicción, el reino y la perseverancia. Fue a causa de la palabra de Dios y del testimonio de Jesús que llegué a estar en la isla llamada Patmos.
es.R: Soy Juan, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} hermano. Como pertenecemos a Jesús, compartimos los mismos sufrimientos. Compartimos {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reino, y compartimos la fuerza para seguir adelante. Yo estaba en la isla de Patmos porque había anunciado la palabra de Dios y el testimonio de Jesús.

sw.L: Mimi Yohana, ndugu yenu na mshirika mwenzenu katika dhiki na ufalme na uvumilivu katika Yesu, nilikuwa katika kisiwa kinachoitwa Patmo kwa sababu ya neno la Mungu na ushuhuda wa Yesu.
sw.B: Mimi Yohana ni ndugu yenu, na katika Yesu ninashiriki pamoja nanyi dhiki, ufalme, na uvumilivu. Nilikuwa katika kisiwa kinachoitwa Patmo kwa sababu ya neno la Mungu na ushuhuda wa Yesu.
sw.R: Mimi ni Yohana, ndugu yenu. Kwa kuwa sisi ni watu wa Yesu, tunashiriki taabu zile zile. Tunashiriki ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na tunashiriki nguvu ya kuendelea kustahimili. Nilikuwa katika kisiwa cha Patmo kwa sababu nilikuwa nimelihubiri neno la Mungu na ushuhuda wa Yesu.

decisions.choice: one shared life: affliction, kingdom and endurance belong together in Jesus
decisions.reason: One article governs all three nouns, so they are one shared lot: those who are in Jesus share his kingdom now, and with it affliction and the endurance it calls for. "In Jesus" may go with all three or only with "endurance"; it is taken here with all three.

decisions.choice: affliction: the pressure and hardship of following Jesus
alternatives: the great tribulation at the end (7:14)
decisions.reason: θλίψει means pressure, distress or persecution. Here it is something John already shares with the churches, so it is their present suffering, not only the final distress of 7:14.

decisions.choice: Patmos: a small island in the Aegean Sea, off the coast of Asia
decisions.reason: Patmos lies about 60 miles (100 km) southwest of Ephesus. The Romans could banish people to islands, and early Christian writers say John was exiled there, but the text says only why he was there, not how he came.

decisions.choice: because of: John was there on account of his witness, most likely as an exile
alternatives: for the sake of: John went there to preach the word, or to receive this revelation
decisions.reason: διὰ with this case usually gives a cause. In 6:9 and 20:4 the same words, "because of the word of God and the testimony", describe why believers were killed. So John was most likely on Patmos as a punishment for proclaiming the gospel.

decisions.choice: because I had spoken God's word (R)
alternatives: because of the word of God
decisions.reason: Readable gives the cause that the grammar decision takes as most likely. It is marked uncertain because the text does not say outright that John was exiled.

decisions.choice: affliction (L, B); troubles (R)
decisions.reason: "Tribulation" is now used mainly as a name for the end-time distress, which would narrow the meaning (m2). "Affliction" keeps the general sense; Readable uses a plainer word.

decisions.choice: John's account of what he saw in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("je me trouvai", "je vis", "je tombai") and in the passé composé at Readable ("j'ai vu") (for the whole book)
alternatives: passé composé at every level, as in the letters
decisions.reason: Revelation opens as a letter, but from here John tells what happened to him and what he saw. French tells a written account in the passé simple, and the style guide asks for it at Literal and Balanced; Readable uses the passé composé, as spoken French and young readers do. Speech inside the visions, such as the seven messages, keeps its own tenses at every level.

decisions.choice: "la détresse" (L, B); "les souffrances" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English avoids "tribulation", French avoids "la tribulation", which is church language and is now often read as the name of an end-time period (m2). "La détresse" names the pressure and hardship of following Jesus; Readable uses a plainer word.

decisions.choice: la aflicción ... la perseverancia (L, B); sufrimientos ... la fuerza para seguir adelante (R)
decisions.reason: "Aflicción" follows the English "affliction" and is the word the Spanish letters already use for the hardship believers suffer (Colossians 1:24, Ephesians 3:13); "tribulación" would sound like a technical term for the end times. "Paciencia" would suggest calm waiting; "perseverancia" is staying firm under pressure, the sense of the Greek word.

decisions.choice: dhiki; uvumilivu (L, B); taabu; kuendelea kustahimili (R)
decisions.reason: "Dhiki" is pressure and hardship, the word for this affliction through the book (m2); "mateso" would narrow it to torture or suffering. "Uvumilivu" for endurance, as in Romans 5:3 and 2 Peter 1:6.

source.text: ἐγενόμην ἐν πνεύματι ἐν τῇ κυριακῇ ἡμέρᾳ, καὶ ἤκουσα ὀπίσω μου φωνὴν μεγάλην ὡς σάλπιγγος λεγούσης· Ὃ βλέπεις γράψον εἰς βιβλίον καὶ πέμψον ταῖς ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαις, εἰς Ἔφεσον καὶ εἰς Σμύρναν καὶ εἰς Πέργαμον καὶ εἰς Θυάτειρα καὶ εἰς Σάρδεις καὶ εἰς Φιλαδέλφειαν καὶ εἰς Λαοδίκειαν.

records.literal_gloss: I came to be in spirit in the Lord's day, and I heard behind me a voice great as of a trumpet \v 11 saying: What you see write into a book and send to the seven churches, to Ephesus and to Smyrna and to Pergamum and to Thyatira and to Sardis and to Philadelphia and to Laodicea.

en.L: I came to be in [the] Spirit on the Lord's day, and I heard behind me a loud voice like [that] of a trumpet, \v 11 saying, "What you see, write in a scroll and send [it] to the seven churches: to Ephesus and to Smyrna and to Pergamum and to Thyatira and to Sardis and to Philadelphia and to Laodicea."
en.B: On the Lord's day I came to be in the Spirit, and from behind me I heard a loud voice that sounded like a trumpet. \v 11 It said, "Write in a scroll what you are seeing, and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea."
en.R: It was the Lord's day, and the Spirit took hold of me. I heard a loud voice behind me. It sounded like a trumpet. \v 11 The voice said, "Write down in a scroll what you see. Then send it to the seven churches in these cities: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea."

fr.L: Je me trouvai dans l’Esprit au jour du Seigneur, et j’entendis derrière moi une voix forte comme [celle] d’une trompette, \v 11 qui disait : « Ce que tu vois, écris-le dans un rouleau et envoie-le aux sept églises : à Éphèse et à Smyrne et à Pergame et à Thyatire et à Sardes et à Philadelphie et à Laodicée. »
fr.B: Le jour du Seigneur, je me trouvai dans l’Esprit, et j’entendis derrière moi une voix forte, pareille au son d’une trompette. \v 11 Elle disait : « Écris dans un rouleau ce que tu vois, et envoie-le aux sept églises : à Éphèse, à Smyrne, à Pergame, à Thyatire, à Sardes, à Philadelphie et à Laodicée. »
fr.R: C’était le jour du Seigneur, et l’Esprit s’est emparé de moi. J’ai entendu derrière moi une voix forte. Elle résonnait comme une trompette. \v 11 La voix m’a dit : « Écris dans un rouleau ce que tu vois. Ensuite, envoie-le aux sept églises de ces villes : Éphèse, Smyrne, Pergame, Thyatire, Sardes, Philadelphie et Laodicée. »

es.L: Llegué a estar en [el] Espíritu en el día del Señor, y oí detrás de mí una gran voz, como de trompeta, \v 11 que decía: «Lo que ves, escríbe[lo] en un rollo y envía[lo] a las siete iglesias: a Éfeso y a Esmirna y a Pérgamo y a Tiatira y a Sardis y a Filadelfia y a Laodicea».
es.B: En el día del Señor me encontré en el Espíritu, y oí detrás de mí una voz fuerte que sonaba como una trompeta. \v 11 Decía: «Escribe en un rollo lo que estás viendo y envíalo a las siete iglesias: a Éfeso, Esmirna, Pérgamo, Tiatira, Sardis, Filadelfia y Laodicea».
es.R: Era el día del Señor, y el Espíritu se apoderó de mí. Oí detrás de mí una voz fuerte. Sonaba como una trompeta. \v 11 La voz dijo: «Escribe en un rollo lo que ves. Luego envíalo a las siete iglesias que están en estas ciudades: Éfeso, Esmirna, Pérgamo, Tiatira, Sardis, Filadelfia y Laodicea».

sw.L: Nilikuwa katika Roho siku ya Bwana, nikasikia nyuma yangu sauti kubwa kama ya tarumbeta, \v 11 ikisema, "Unachokiona, kiandike katika gombo, ukalipeleke kwa makanisa saba: kwa Efeso na kwa Smirna na kwa Pergamo na kwa Thiatira na kwa Sardi na kwa Filadelfia na kwa Laodikia."
sw.B: Siku ya Bwana nilikuwa katika Roho, nikasikia nyuma yangu sauti kubwa iliyosikika kama tarumbeta. \v 11 Ilisema, "Andika katika gombo kile unachokiona, ukalipeleke kwa makanisa saba: Efeso, Smirna, Pergamo, Thiatira, Sardi, Filadelfia na Laodikia."
sw.R: Ilikuwa siku ya Bwana, na Roho akanishika. Nilisikia sauti kubwa nyuma yangu. Ilisikika kama tarumbeta. \v 11 Sauti hiyo ilisema, "Andika katika gombo kile unachokiona. Kisha lipeleke kwa makanisa saba yaliyo katika miji hii: Efeso, Smirna, Pergamo, Thiatira, Sardi, Filadelfia na Laodikia."

decisions.choice: in the Spirit: under the power of God's Spirit, able to see visions
alternatives: in a trance, a state of the human spirit
decisions.reason: πνεύματι has no article and could describe John's own state, "in spirit". But in Revelation the visions come by the Spirit of God (4:2; 17:3; 21:10), as they did for Ezekiel (Ezekiel 3:12-14; 11:1), so it is taken here as the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: the Lord's day: the first day of the week, when Christians met
alternatives: the day of the Lord, the day of judgment, into which John is carried in vision
decisions.reason: κυριακῇ is an adjective, "belonging to the Lord", the same word Paul uses of the Lord's supper (1 Corinthians 11:20). Christian writers from soon after use "the Lord's day" for Sunday, the day of the resurrection, when believers gathered (compare Acts 20:7). The Old Testament "day of the Lord" is a different phrase.

decisions.choice: a scroll: a written roll, the usual form of a book
decisions.reason: βιβλίον means a written document. In John's day books were written on rolls of papyrus or parchment; bound books were just coming into use. Revelation later speaks of scrolls that are rolled up and sealed (5:1; 6:14).

decisions.choice: seven cities on a road through the province of Asia
decisions.reason: The seven cities lie in the order a messenger would reach them on a circuit, starting at Ephesus on the coast and going north, then east and south. Chapters 2-3 hold the message to each church in the same order.

decisions.choice: scroll (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: "Book" makes an English reader picture a bound volume. "Scroll" names the object John would have used (m3).

decisions.choice: the Spirit took hold of me (R)
decisions.reason: "In the Spirit" is not plain English for a young reader. Readable says what it means: John was under the Spirit's power. It depends on the uncertain decision m1.

decisions.choice: "un rouleau" (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in English, "un livre" makes a reader picture a bound volume; "un rouleau" names the object John would have written on (m3). The same word is used for the scroll with seven seals in chapter 5.

decisions.choice: rollo
decisions.reason: A "libro" today is a bound book with pages; the Greek word here is a written roll, the usual form of a book then. "Rollo" keeps that picture, which matters again in chapter 5.

decisions.choice: Éfeso, Esmirna, Pérgamo, Tiatira, Sardis, Filadelfia, Laodicea
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish forms of the seven city names. "Sardis" is the form most Spanish readers know; "Sardes" is also used.

decisions.choice: Efeso, Smirna, Pergamo, Thiatira, Sardi, Filadelfia, Laodikia
decisions.reason: The usual Swahili forms of the seven city names; Efeso (Ephesians 1:1), Thiatira (Acts 16:14) and Laodikia (Colossians 2:1) as already used in the Swahili New Testament. The same through chapters 2 and 3.

decisions.choice: gombo
decisions.reason: "Gombo" is a written roll, the Swahili word for scroll used in Luke 4:17; "kitabu" would suggest a bound book (m3).

source.text: Καὶ ἐπέστρεψα βλέπειν τὴν φωνὴν ἥτις ἐλάλει μετ’ ἐμοῦ· καὶ ἐπιστρέψας εἶδον ἑπτὰ λυχνίας χρυσᾶς, καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τῶν λυχνιῶν ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, ἐνδεδυμένον ποδήρη καὶ περιεζωσμένον πρὸς τοῖς μαστοῖς ζώνην χρυσᾶν·

records.literal_gloss: And I turned to see the voice which was speaking with me; and having turned I saw seven lampstands golden, \v 13 and in [the] middle of the lampstands [one] like a son of man, having been clothed [in a robe] reaching-to-the-feet and having been girded at the breasts [with] a sash golden;

en.L: And I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me, and having turned I saw seven golden lampstands, \v 13 and in [the] middle of the lampstands [one] like a son of man, clothed [in a robe reaching] to the feet and wrapped around at the chest [with] a golden sash.
en.B: I turned around to see whose voice it was that spoke with me, and as I turned I saw seven lampstands made of gold. \v 13 In the middle of the lampstands was one like a son of man. A long robe came down to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, and a gold sash was tied around {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chest.
en.R: I turned around to see who was speaking to me. When I turned, I saw seven lampstands made of gold. \v 13 Someone was standing among the lampstands. He looked like a son of man, a human being. He was wearing a long robe that came down to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. A gold sash was tied across {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chest.

fr.L: Et je me retournai pour voir la voix qui parlait avec moi ; et m’étant retourné, je vis sept chandeliers d’or, \v 13 et au milieu des chandeliers [quelqu’un] semblable à un fils d’homme, vêtu [d’une robe descendant] jusqu’aux pieds et ceint à la poitrine d’une ceinture d’or.
fr.B: Je me retournai pour voir de qui venait la voix qui me parlait, et en me retournant je vis sept chandeliers d’or. \v 13 Au milieu des chandeliers se tenait quelqu’un qui ressemblait à un fils d’homme. Il portait une longue robe qui descendait jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, et une ceinture d’or était nouée autour de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} poitrine.
fr.R: Je me suis retourné pour voir qui me parlait. En me retournant, j’ai vu sept chandeliers en or. \v 13 Quelqu’un se tenait au milieu des chandeliers. Il ressemblait à un fils d’homme, c’est-à-dire à un être humain. Il portait une longue robe qui descendait jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds. Une ceinture en or était attachée sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} poitrine.

es.L: Y me volví para ver la voz que hablaba conmigo; y habiéndome vuelto, vi siete candelabros de oro, \v 13 y en medio de los candelabros [a uno] semejante a un hijo de hombre, vestido [con una túnica que llegaba] hasta los pies y ceñido a la altura del pecho [con] un cinto de oro.
es.B: Me di la vuelta para ver de quién era la voz que hablaba conmigo, y al volverme vi siete candelabros de oro. \v 13 En medio de los candelabros estaba uno semejante a un hijo de hombre. Llevaba una túnica larga que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} llegaba hasta los pies, y un cinto de oro ceñido al pecho.
es.R: Me di la vuelta para ver quién me hablaba. Al volverme, vi siete candelabros de oro. \v 13 Entre los candelabros había alguien de pie. Parecía un hijo de hombre, un ser humano. Llevaba puesta una túnica larga que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} llegaba hasta los pies. Tenía un cinto de oro atado sobre el pecho.

sw.L: Na nikageuka ili kuiona sauti iliyokuwa ikisema nami; na nilipogeuka niliona vinara saba vya taa vya dhahabu, \v 13 na katikati ya vinara [mmoja] aliye kama mwana wa mtu, amevaa [vazi refu hadi] miguuni, na amefungwa mshipi wa dhahabu kifuani.
sw.B: Niligeuka nione ni sauti ya nani iliyokuwa ikisema nami, na nilipogeuka niliona vinara saba vya taa vilivyotengenezwa kwa dhahabu. \v 13 Katikati ya vinara hivyo alikuwapo mmoja aliye kama mwana wa mtu. Alikuwa amevaa vazi refu lililofika miguuni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, na mshipi wa dhahabu ulikuwa umefungwa kifuani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.
sw.R: Niligeuka nimwone aliyekuwa akisema nami. Nilipogeuka, niliona vinara saba vya taa vilivyotengenezwa kwa dhahabu. \v 13 Mtu fulani alikuwa amesimama katikati ya vinara hivyo. Alionekana kama mwana wa mtu, yaani mwanadamu. Alikuwa amevaa vazi refu lililofika miguuni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Mshipi wa dhahabu ulikuwa umefungwa kifuani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.

decisions.choice: turned to see the voice: turned to see who was speaking
decisions.reason: To "see the voice" is a vivid way of saying that John turned to see the speaker.

decisions.choice: lampstands like the lampstand of the tabernacle and of Zechariah's vision
decisions.reason: A λυχνίας held oil lamps. The tabernacle had one gold lampstand with seven lamps (Exodus 25:31-40), and Zechariah saw one in a vision (Zechariah 4:2). Here there are seven, and 1:20 says they are the seven churches.

decisions.choice: one like a son of man: the figure of Daniel 7:13
alternatives: the title "the Son of Man" as Jesus used it in the Gospels
decisions.reason: ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, with no article, repeats Daniel 7:13, where "one like a son of man" means a figure in human form who receives God's kingdom. It is not quite the Gospels' title, "the Son of Man", which has the article, but it points to the same person: verses 17-18 show that he is Jesus.

decisions.choice: a long robe and a gold sash: dress of a priest, and of the heavenly figure in Daniel 10
decisions.reason: ποδήρη is a robe reaching to the feet. In the Greek Old Testament the same word is used for the high priest's robe (Exodus 28:4), and the man Daniel saw was clothed in linen with a belt of gold (Daniel 10:5). The dress suggests priestly and royal dignity; the text does not say more.

decisions.choice: whose voice it was (B); who was speaking (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "to see the voice"; Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1).

decisions.choice: a son of man, lowercase (L, B, R); someone who looked human (R)
decisions.reason: Every level writes "a son of man" in lowercase, as Daniel 7:13 has it (m3), and Readable adds that the phrase means a human figure.

decisions.choice: lampstands
decisions.reason: These held oil lamps, not candles, so "lampstands" is the accurate word at every level.

decisions.choice: chest
decisions.reason: μαστοῖς here means the chest; the sash was worn high, not at the waist. "Chest" says this in plain English at every level.

decisions.choice: "chandeliers" (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The English avoids anything that suggests candles. In French Bible language "chandelier" is the established word for the lampstand of the tabernacle and of Zechariah's vision (m2), which held oil lamps; "porte-lampes" is exact but rare and would hide that link. A native reviewer may prefer "porte-lampes".

decisions.choice: candelabros
decisions.reason: These are stands that hold lamps, like the lampstand of the tabernacle; "candelabro" is the word Hebrews 9:2 already uses for it. "Candelero" now usually means a holder for a single candle, and "lámpara" would name the light rather than the stand.

decisions.choice: semejante a un hijo de hombre (lowercase)
decisions.reason: John describes what he sees in the words of Daniel 7:13, without the article, so Spanish keeps it lowercase and indefinite, as the English does. "El Hijo del Hombre" is kept for Jesus's own title in the Gospels.

decisions.choice: mwana wa mtu, lowercase
decisions.reason: Here the phrase describes the figure of Daniel 7:13, one who looks human (m3), so Swahili says "mwana wa mtu" (a son of a human being) in lowercase, as the English keeps "a son of man" lowercase. The Gospels' title "Mwana wa Adamu" would make the vision name him instead of describing him. A reviewer may prefer the title, which links the passage with Jesus's own words.

decisions.choice: vinara vya taa
decisions.reason: "Kinara cha taa" is a lampstand, as in Hebrews 9:2; the plural "vinara vya taa" is used through the book.

source.text: ἡ δὲ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ αἱ τρίχες λευκαὶ ὡς ἔριον λευκόν, ὡς χιών, καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ὡς φλὸξ πυρός, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὅμοιοι χαλκολιβάνῳ, ὡς ἐν καμίνῳ πεπυρωμένης, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ αὐτοῦ ὡς φωνὴ ὑδάτων πολλῶν, καὶ ἔχων ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ ἀστέρας ἑπτά, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ῥομφαία δίστομος ὀξεῖα ἐκπορευομένη, καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος φαίνει ἐν τῇ δυνάμει αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And the head of him and the hairs white as wool white, as snow, and the eyes of him as flame of fire \v 15 and the feet of him like to fine-bronze as in a furnace having been fired, and the voice of him as [the] voice of waters many, \v 16 and having in the right hand of him stars seven, and out of the mouth of him a sword two-mouthed sharp going out, and the face of him as the sun shines in the power of it.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head and hair [were] white like white wool, like snow, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes like a flame of fire, \v 15 and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet like fine bronze, as [if] fired in a furnace, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice like [the] voice of many waters, \v 16 and holding in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand seven stars, and out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth a sharp two-edged sword going out, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face like the sun shines in its strength.
en.B: His head and hair were white as wool is white, white as snow, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes were like flaming fire. \v 15 His feet were like fine bronze, fired as in a furnace, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice sounded like many waters. \v 16 Seven stars were in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand, a sharp sword with two edges came out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face was as bright as the sun when it shines with all its strength.
en.R: His head and hair were as white as wool or snow. His eyes blazed like fire. \v 15 His feet shone like bronze that has been heated in a furnace. His voice was like the roar of a mighty flood. \v 16 He held seven stars in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand. A sharp sword with two edges came out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth. His face shone as brightly as the midday sun.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} cheveux [étaient] blancs comme de la laine blanche, comme de la neige, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux comme une flamme de feu, \v 15 et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds semblables à du bronze fin, comme embrasé dans une fournaise, et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} voix comme la voix d’eaux nombreuses, \v 16 et ayant dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main droite sept étoiles, et de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche sortant une épée aiguë à deux tranchants, et {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} visage comme le soleil brille dans sa force.
fr.B: Sa tête et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} cheveux étaient blancs comme de la laine blanche, blancs comme la neige, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux étaient comme une flamme ardente. \v 15 Ses pieds étaient semblables à du bronze fin, embrasé comme dans une fournaise, et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} voix était comme le grondement d’eaux nombreuses. \v 16 Il tenait sept étoiles dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main droite, une épée aiguë à deux tranchants sortait de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche, et {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} visage était aussi éclatant que le soleil quand il brille de toute sa force.
fr.R: Sa tête et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} cheveux étaient blancs comme la laine ou la neige. Ses yeux flamboyaient comme du feu. \v 15 Ses pieds étincelaient comme du bronze chauffé dans un four. Sa voix grondait comme un grand fleuve en crue. \v 16 Il tenait sept étoiles dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main droite. Une épée bien aiguisée, à deux tranchants, sortait de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche. Son visage brillait comme le soleil en plein midi.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} cabellos [eran] blancos como lana blanca, como nieve, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ojos como llama de fuego, \v 15 y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies semejantes a bronce bruñido, como refinado en un horno, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz como [el] estruendo de muchas aguas, \v 16 y tenía en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano derecha siete estrellas, y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca salía una espada aguda de dos filos, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} rostro [era] como el sol cuando brilla con toda su fuerza.
es.B: Tenía la cabeza y el cabello blancos como la lana blanca, blancos como la nieve, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ojos eran como llama de fuego. \v 15 Sus pies eran como bronce bruñido, refinado como en un horno, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz sonaba como muchas aguas. \v 16 En {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano derecha tenía siete estrellas, de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca salía una espada aguda de dos filos, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} rostro brillaba como el sol cuando resplandece con toda su fuerza.
es.R: Su cabeza y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabello eran tan blancos como la lana o la nieve. Sus ojos ardían como fuego. \v 15 Sus pies brillaban como bronce calentado en un horno. Su voz era como el rugido de una gran inundación. \v 16 Tenía siete estrellas en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano derecha. De {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca salía una espada aguda de dos filos. Su rostro brillaba tanto como el sol del mediodía.

sw.L: Kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} na nywele [zake zilikuwa] nyeupe kama sufu nyeupe, kama theluji, na macho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kama mwali wa moto, \v 15 na miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kama shaba bora, kana kwamba imepashwa moto katika tanuru, na sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kama sauti ya maji mengi, \v 16 naye akiwa ameshika katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia nyota saba, na kutoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}} ukitoka upanga mkali wenye makali kuwili, na uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kama jua linavyong'aa kwa nguvu zake.
sw.B: Kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} na nywele {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} vilikuwa vyeupe kama sufu, vyeupe kama theluji, na macho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yalikuwa kama moto unaowaka. \v 15 Miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilikuwa kama shaba bora iliyopashwa moto katika tanuru, na sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilikuwa kama sauti ya maji mengi. \v 16 Alikuwa ameshika nyota saba katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia, upanga mkali wenye makali kuwili ulitoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, na uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ulikuwa ukiangaza kama jua linapong'aa kwa nguvu zake zote.
sw.R: Kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} na nywele {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} vilikuwa vyeupe kama sufu au theluji. Macho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yaling'aa kama moto. \v 15 Miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilimeta kama shaba iliyopashwa moto katika tanuru. Sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilikuwa kama ngurumo ya mafuriko makubwa. \v 16 Alishika nyota saba katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia. Upanga mkali wenye makali kuwili ulitoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} uling'aa kama jua la mchana.

decisions.choice: the description draws on Daniel 7 and 10
decisions.reason: White hair like wool belongs in Daniel 7:9 to the Ancient of Days, God himself; here it belongs to the one like a son of man. Eyes like flames of fire, feet like burnished bronze and a voice like the sound of a multitude come from Daniel 10:6, and a voice like the sound of many waters from Ezekiel 43:2, where it is the voice of the God of Israel. The figure has both human form and the marks of God's glory.

decisions.choice: fine bronze: a highly polished metal alloy, glowing as if fired
decisions.reason: χαλκολιβάνῳ is found nowhere before Revelation (also 2:18), and its exact meaning is not known. It is clearly a bright metal, probably a fine alloy of copper, like the polished bronze of Daniel 10:6 and Ezekiel 1:7.

decisions.choice: as if it had been fired in a furnace
decisions.reason: πεπυρωμένης does not agree in form with the word for furnace, and the manuscripts differ here. The sense is clear: the feet glow like metal refined in a furnace. Reviewers should check the variants against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: seven stars: the angels of the seven churches
decisions.reason: Verse 20 explains them. Holding them in his right hand shows that the churches' angels are in his power and care (2:1).

decisions.choice: a sword from the mouth: his word that judges
decisions.reason: ῥομφαία is a long sword. A sword coming from the mouth stands for the power of his word, as in Isaiah 11:4 and 49:2 and Hebrews 4:12. Revelation uses it again for his judgment (2:12, 16; 19:15, 21). The text gives a picture; it is not describing a literal sword.

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable break the list into sentences
decisions.reason: The Greek runs the whole description as one list, with "and" between each part and no verbs for most of them. Balanced and Readable supply the verbs ("were", "came", "shone") and divide it into sentences.

decisions.choice: sounded like many waters (B); a mighty flood (R)
decisions.reason: φωνὴ means both voice and sound. Balanced keeps "many waters" and makes the voice a sound; Readable uses a picture young readers know.

decisions.choice: bronce bruñido
decisions.reason: The Greek word names a fine, highly polished bronze; "bruñido" says the metal has been polished until it shines, the picture of the meaning decision. Readable says only that the feet shone like heated bronze.

decisions.choice: shaba bora
decisions.reason: The Greek word names a fine, highly polished metal alloy (m2) whose exact makeup is unknown; "shaba bora" (fine bronze) says that without guessing at the alloy.

source.text: Καὶ ὅτε εἶδον αὐτόν, ἔπεσα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ὡς νεκρός· καὶ ἔθηκεν τὴν δεξιὰν αὐτοῦ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ λέγων· Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος, καὶ ὁ ζῶν καὶ ἐγενόμην νεκρὸς καὶ ἰδοὺ ζῶν εἰμι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων καὶ ἔχω τὰς κλεῖς τοῦ θανάτου καὶ τοῦ ᾅδου.

records.literal_gloss: And when I saw him, I fell toward the feet of him as dead; and he placed the right of him on me saying: Not fear; I am the first and the last \v 18 and the living [one], and I became dead and behold living I am into the ages of the ages, and I have the keys of the death and of the Hades.

en.L: And when I saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, I fell at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet as [though] dead. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} placed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right [hand] on me, saying, "Do not be afraid; I am the first and the last \v 18 and the living one, and I became dead, and look, I am alive for the ages of the ages, and I have the keys of death and of Hades.
en.B: At the sight of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} I fell down at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet like a dead man. He laid {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand on me and said, "Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last \v 18 and the one who lives. I was dead, and see, I am alive for all the ages to come, and the keys of death and Hades are {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.
en.R: When I saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, I fell to the ground at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. I lay there as if I were dead. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand on me and said, "Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last. I was there before all things, and I will be there after all things. \v 18 I am the one who lives. I was dead, but look! Now I am alive forever and ever. I hold the keys to death and to the place of the dead.

fr.L: Et quand je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} vis, je tombai à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds comme mort ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} posa {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} [main] droite sur moi, en disant : « N’aie pas peur ; je suis le premier et le dernier, \v 18 et le vivant ; et je suis devenu mort, et voici, je suis vivant pour les siècles des siècles, et j’ai les clés de la mort et de l’Hadès.
fr.B: Quand je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} vis, je tombai à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds comme un mort. Il posa {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main droite sur moi et dit : « N’aie pas peur. Je suis le premier et le dernier, \v 18 celui qui vit. J’étais mort, et voici, je suis vivant pour tous les siècles à venir, et les clés de la mort et du séjour des morts sont à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Quand je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ai vu, je suis tombé à terre, à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds. Je restais là, comme mort. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a posé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main droite sur moi et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a dit : « N’aie pas peur. Je suis le premier et le dernier. J’existais avant toutes choses, et j’existerai après toutes choses. \v 18 Je suis celui qui vit. J’étais mort, mais regarde ! Maintenant, je suis vivant pour toujours et à jamais. Je tiens les clés de la mort et du séjour des morts.

es.L: Y cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vi, caí a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies como muerto. Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} [mano] derecha sobre mí, diciendo: «No temas; yo soy el primero y el último \v 18 y el que vive, y estuve muerto, y mira, estoy vivo por los siglos de los siglos, y tengo las llaves de la muerte y del Hades.
es.B: Al verlo, caí a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies como un muerto. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano derecha sobre mí y dijo: «No tengas miedo. Yo soy el primero y el último \v 18 y el que vive. Estuve muerto, y ya ves: estoy vivo por los siglos de los siglos, y las llaves de la muerte y del Hades son {{deity_pronoun:mías|Mías}}.
es.R: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vi, caí al suelo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies. Quedé tendido como si estuviera muerto. Entonces {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano derecha sobre mí y me dijo: «No tengas miedo. Yo soy el primero y el último. Yo estaba antes de todas las cosas, y estaré después de todas ellas. \v 18 Yo soy el que vive. Estuve muerto, pero ¡mira! Ahora estoy vivo para siempre. Tengo las llaves de la muerte y del lugar de los muertos.

sw.L: Na nilipomwona, nilianguka miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} kama mfu. Naye akaweka [mkono] {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia juu yangu, akisema, "Usiogope; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni wa kwanza na wa mwisho, \v 18 na aliye hai; nikawa mfu, na tazama, niko hai hata zama za zama, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nina funguo za kifo na za Kuzimu.
